summary: Box-free wave 5: readers for the unread regions (config/boot resolve, ae event loop + beforeSleepIO shape, io-uring reply/recv paths) + independent adversarial verification of the SPSC staged-dirty-bitmap ordering argument.

candidates.change: Replace the fixed 100us poll while replyWorking>0 with an adaptive drain: N passes of zero-timeout epoll_pwait2 (or a bounded ~5-20us spin re-running beforesleep) before falling back to the 100us window. Numeric knob (spin budget in us, 0=off) per knob philosophy. Also delete the empty 'if (replyWorking == 0){ }' branch.
candidates.mechanism: After dispatch, workers typically finish in ~1-5us but the IO thread sleeps the full 100us unless an unrelated fd event arrives - at low pipeline / single client nothing arrives until the reply is sent, so every request eats up to 100us of idle sleep (this IS the low-pipeline latency floor the pwait2 comment describes; pwait2 only shaved it from 1ms to 100us). IO cores are dedicated and pinned (S2), so a short spin costs nothing anyone else wanted; zero-timeout polls still service fd events each pass so no starvation.
candidates.risk: Burns the pinned core while spinning (acceptable, dedicated); must cap the spin so a wedged worker doesn't turn the IO thread into a pure busy-loop; keep gated so power/thermal-sensitive runs can zero it.

candidates.change: Lazy EPOLLOUT removal: when writeToClient drains with handler_installed, don't connSetWriteHandler(NULL) immediately - mark the conn write-idle and let the NEXT writable event delete the handler iff still nothing pending (first spurious fire deletes). A re-install before that event just clears the mark (the func==write_handler short-circuit at socket.c:229 already makes re-arm free).
candidates.mechanism: Send-bound streaming (16KB replies, the regime where per-reply partial writes are the norm) currently pays two epoll_ctl(MOD) syscalls per reply: install on partial (networking.c:3747 / sendReplyToClient path), delete on drain (networking.c:3256). With back-to-back replies the delete+re-add pair collapses to zero epoll_ctls in steady state; only the final drain pays one spurious wakeup + one delete.
candidates.risk: Level-triggered epoll: MUST delete on the first spurious writable event or the fd storms the loop; audit interactions with AE_BARRIER (aof always-fsync), CLIENT_PROTECTED (protectClient sets NULL handler expecting removal), and freeClient teardown (aeDeleteFileEvent on close already covers the armed case).

candidates.change: Dirty-queue bitmap for flushExQueues: exQueuePush sets bit w in a per-IO-thread (iotid-indexed, producer-private) uint64 when it advances staged_tail; flushExQueues walks only set bits via ctz and clears the mask, instead of loading q->tail/staged_tail for all num_workers queues.
candidates.mechanism: flushExQueues runs at the top of EVERY beforeSleepIO iteration AND at the end of every processInputBuffer batch (networking.c:4683). Each call touches num_workers exQueue structs spread across the exThread array - nw distinct cache lines (tail lines are also read by consumers, so they're frequently in S state or evicted) even when nothing was staged, e.g. every idle-poll wakeup while replyWorking>0. Bitmap makes the no-op case one TLS load.
candidates.risk: Low - bitmap is single-threaded (only the owning IO thread pushes/flushes its queues); must mirror into both canonical forks and cap at 64 workers or use two words; verify main thread (iotid 0) TLS init.

candidates.change: beforeSleepIO no-pending early-outs bundle: (a) handleClientsWithPendingWrites - check listLength(clients_pending_write[iotid])==0 and return BEFORE the server.io_uring_net && iouEnsureRing(iotid) gate; (b) cache at init whether ANY conn type implements process_pending_data (only TLS does) and skip the connTypeProcessPendingData call + CONN_TYPE_MAX pointer-walk entirely on plain-TCP builds; (c) delete the dead aeSetAfterSleepProc(t->el, afterSleepIO) at server.c:10687 - aeProcessEventsIO never calls aftersleep, so afterSleepIO/updateCachedTime is unreachable on IO threads.
candidates.mechanism: Every loop iteration (10k/s per IO thread while replies in flight) pays: a global load + state check for the uring gate, a 4-slot function-pointer walk that is always a no-op without TLS, and carries a dead registration that misleads readers into thinking cached time updates per IO wakeup. Each shave is a few ns but they sit on the highest-frequency path in the server.
candidates.risk: Minimal; (b) needs the flag recomputed if TLS can be enabled at runtime (connTypeInitialize order); (c) is pure dead-code removal - or, if updateCachedTime on IO threads was INTENDED, that's a separate latent issue (racy global stores) better left deleted anyway.

candidates.change: Track a per-client producer-private active-cdb set (bitmap over cdb indices, set at dispatch when a fake targets cdb c, bit cleared when no in-flight slot uses it) and have cdbCombinedMask scan only those indices instead of all server.num_cdb.
candidates.mechanism: With multi-cdb ON (#75: num_cdb = min(num_workers,256)), the drain does num_cdb acquire loads over num_cdb cache-line-isolated buses PER pending client PER beforeSleepIO pass - including clients whose in-flight commands all target one worker (the common single-shard case) and passes where nothing completed. A client pipelining to 1 worker with 8 workers configured pays 8 line touches per pass for 1 useful bit. Dispatch and drain both run on the owning IO thread, so the tracking set needs no atomics.
candidates.risk: Moderate: the set must be exact-or-superset of live cdbs or a completion is missed (hang) - clearing logic must handle wraparound of flushid/dispatchid and cross-shard heads whose completion bit is set by the LAST sub; only pays off when tomokv-num-cdb > 0 (default 0 => num_cdb==1, single load, no gain).

candidates.change: Cache the earliest-timer deadline (already computed by usUntilEarliestTimer before the poll, and maintainable on aeCreateTimeEvent/timer re-arm) and skip the processTimeEvents list walk when getMonotonicUs() < cached deadline; ideally reuse one time read per iteration.
candidates.mechanism: IO threads pay zero timer cost (aeProcessEventsIO has no time events - confirmed good). But the MAIN thread - which is also client-serving IO thread 0 - runs full aeProcessEvents every iteration: usUntilEarliestTimer O(N-timers) walk + processTimeEvents full walk + at least two getMonotonicUs vDSO calls, even when the poll returned in microseconds for fd events and serverCron isn't due for ~10ms. With only serverCron (+module timers) N is small, so this is a per-iteration constant shave on iotid 0's throughput, not a structural fix.
candidates.risk: Low mechanically (deadline cache invalidation on create/delete/re-arm is simple), but expect small absolute gain unless module timers inflate N; measure on iotid-0-heavy configs before keeping.

candidates.change: exBindNumaLocal() gates on `if (server.pin_mode != 1) return;` — it runs ONLY in manual pin mode. Every other reference promises the opposite: the declaration comment (server.c:118) says "pin_mode==2 (auto)", the call-site comment (server.c:10232) says "no-op unless pin_mode==2 auto", and README.md:224 advertises "NUMA-local shard memory" as part of auto mode 2. Flip the gate to ==2, and derive the node from sched_getcpu() instead of smartCoreFor(ex_id).
candidates.mechanism: Double inversion: (a) in the DEFAULT pin-mode (2=auto) NUMA-local shard-memory binding never runs, so the documented multi-NUMA EPYC/Threadripper win silently doesn't exist — exactly the machine class the final-server plan targets; (b) when it does run (manual mode 1), the node is computed from smartCoreFor(ex_id), the AUTO-mode core map, while manual mode actually pinned the worker to g_man[idx % g_nman] — so set_mempolicy can prefer a REMOTE node, actively pessimizing the shard. The function's own header comment says getcpu() from the already-pinned thread is the correct source; the code never calls it.
candidates.risk: Low. One-line gate flip + replace smartCoreFor with sched_getcpu() (comment already asserts the thread is pinned when called). Behavior change only on multi-node boxes; MPOL_PREFERRED falls back rather than OOMs. Verify no bench baseline depended on the (accidental) manual-mode-only behavior.

candidates.file_line: /shared/Projects/THredis-2s-improve/src/server.c:10988 vs 11009 (window: 10671-10694 create+arm per-IO-thread listeners; deref at 5718/5768 csPushSpin)
candidates.change: initIOThreads() is called (main:10988) before initExThreads() (main:11009), and each spawned IO thread creates its own SO_REUSEPORT listening socket, registers the accept handler, and starts its event loop INSIDE initIOThreads — so IO threads 1..N-1 accept and execute client commands while server.exThreads is still NULL and before ACLLoadUsersAtStartup (11002), module load (10999-11000), and InitServerLast (11007). Either move initExThreads before initIOThreads, or defer listener-socket creation/arming into initListeners after all init completes.
candidates.mechanism: A client that connects in the multi-millisecond window (ACL load + module load + cluster init sit inside it) and sends any sharded command reaches dispatch, which has no NULL guard: `sub->db = &server.exThreads[w].db[dbid]` / csPushSpin's `&server.exThreads[w].queues[iotid]` dereference NULL → segfault at boot. Secondary: commands are servable before ACL users are loaded (auth against default-only ACL) — upstream Redis deliberately opens listeners last; this fork's per-thread listeners broke that invariant. This is classic init-order fragility: it never fires in benchmarks (load-gen starts after "Ready to accept") but fires with systemd socket-activation-style eager clients or restart-under-load.
candidates.risk: Medium-low. initExThreads only needs num_workers/ex_dbs/io_threads (all set in initServer), so hoisting it above initIOThreads is safe (worker loops spin on empty queues); alternatively arming accept handlers late is a smaller diff but touches the SO_REUSEPORT setup. Check exThreadMain doesn't touch module/ACL state at idle (it doesn't — it pops queues and prefetches).

candidates.file_line: /shared/Projects/THredis-2s-improve/src/server.c:3309-3324 (bypasses: config.c:3216 appendonly/updateAppendonly, config.c:3370 maxmemory/updateMaxmemory, config.c:3386 maxmemory-clients, activedefrag; REPLICAOF command)
candidates.change: The RP-1 role-purity gate ("refuse configs that silently lose or corrupt SHARD data") is enforced ONLY at initServer. All five guarded settings are MODIFIABLE_CONFIG and their apply fns (updateAppendonly, updateMaxmemory, applyClientMaxMemoryUsage) contain no num_workers check, and REPLICAOF is a runtime command. Add the same num_workers>0 rejection to the apply/validate path (and to replicaofCommand), or mark these IMMUTABLE-when-sharded.
candidates.mechanism: The gate's own comment promises "fail loud at startup rather than corrupt silently," but `CONFIG SET appendonly yes` one second after boot starts an AOF that serializes only the empty decoy server.db (total data loss on reload); `CONFIG SET maxmemory 1gb` arms eviction that can free nothing real (permanent OOM write-stop with N IO threads racing the shared eviction pool); REPLICAOF ships an empty dataset — precisely the corruption modes RP-1 enumerates, reachable through the front door at runtime. Boot-time-only enforcement of an invariant that is mutable at runtime is the gap.
candidates.risk: Low. Guard additions in three apply fns + one command; error string can reuse the RP-1 wording. No hot-path impact. Must keep the boot path working (apply fns don't run during loadServerConfig, so no boot-order interaction).

candidates.file_line: /shared/Projects/THredis-2s-improve/src/config.c:3173-3178 (consumers gated at networking.c:3295-3702, server.c:10222; no boot guard anywhere)
candidates.change: The six io_uring/worker-send bools (tomokv-io-uring, -sqpoll, -recv, -zc, tomokv-worker-direct-send, tomokv-io-uring-reply-send) are accepted with zero cross-validation: (a) on a non-USE_URING build every consumer is compiled out under #ifdef HAVE_LIBURING, so the knobs silently no-op; (b) io-uring-recv documents "requires io_uring_net" (server.h:2962) but nothing enforces it — recv without net silently never arms (networking.c:435 requires both); (c) io-uring-reply-send without io-uring-net silently degrades to the epoll pending-write path (server.c:2103 → networking.c:3706 falls through). Add a boot resolve block: FATAL (or loud WARNING + forced-off NOTICE) for uring knobs on a non-liburing build, and resolve dependent knobs against io_uring_net with a logged message.
candidates.mechanism: This is the exact failure class already paid for once on the strict fork: 3-stage without USE_URING silently misbehaved and produced the bogus "37% reply race" — that fork got a guard (f3e90ed4c); this fork has none. Silent no-op knobs are a bench-validity trap (you sweep "uring vs epoll" and measure epoll vs epoll) and violate the repo's own knob doctrine that invalid combos fail loud. The other resolved knobs (pipeline-depth, ex-queue-depth) log their resolution; these log nothing.
candidates.risk: Low-medium. FATAL could break existing sweep scripts that pass uring flags to a plain build — a forced-off NOTICE per knob (matching the strict-fork guard style) is the compatible variant. Pure boot-time code.

candidates.file_line: /shared/Projects/THredis-2s-improve/src/server.c:10552-10570 (order contract; parse 10556-10563; wrong log label 10587; mapping defined by pinExToCore:10618 / pinIOThreadToCore:10624-10627)
candidates.change: Manual pin-mode contract bugs: (1) the tomokv-pin-cores comment says the list is applied "io threads first, then workers" but the code maps WORKERS to list slots 0..W-1 and IO threads to W..W+N (pinIOThreadToCore uses num_workers+io_id) — an operator following the comment gets an exactly inverted placement; (2) the pin-cores string is parsed lazily at first pin with a silently-truncating parser (`if (end == p) break;` — a typo like "0;2" yields the list {0} and pins every thread to core 0 with no error) instead of being validated at config-set time; (3) the pin log at 10587 appends "(smart)" for pin_mode==1, but smart/L3 grouping is mode 2. Fix the comment (and README) to the real worker-first order, validate/parse pin-cores in a config validator (fail loud on trailing garbage, on empty-with-mode-1), and fix the label.
candidates.mechanism: pin-mode 1 exists so operators can place threads exactly; a wrong ordering doc plus a parser that silently accepts garbage produces valid-looking boots with pathological placement (all threads on one core, or workers on the intended IO cores) — the failure only shows up as unexplained throughput numbers, which the sanity-gate rule then burns time on. Validation at boot is cheap because the knob is IMMUTABLE.
candidates.risk: Low. Comment/README/log fixes are free; adding a validator could reject configs that previously 'worked' by accident (silent truncation) — that is the point. Parsing once at boot into a server-struct array also removes the static-local lazy-init.

candidates.file_line: /shared/Projects/THredis-2s-improve/src/server.c:3131-3146 + 3332-3338 + 10578-10579 + 10486-10517 (also dead mask 3191; doc drift README.md:227 vs server.h:1832)
candidates.change: Consolidate the triplicated L3-topology probing and make the num_cdb resolve log like its sibling autos: detectL3Domains() is run twice (initServer num_cdb auto; again in pinThreadToCoreN behind a static g_multi_l3 cache) and buildSmartCoreOrder() re-parses L3 topology a THIRD way (level/id files vs shared_cpu_list) — probe once in initServer, store server.detected_l3_domains next to detected_l3_bytes, and have both consumers read it. While there: (a) the num_cdb block logs nothing — neither the auto choice nor the silent cap of an explicit tomokv-num-cdb request to num_workers (pipeline/ex-queue autos both emit NOTICE); (b) detectL3Domains `if (!f) break;` stops at the first CPU lacking cache/index3 (offline cores, nosmt holes) and undercounts domains, flipping BOTH the num_cdb auto and pin auto to single-CCD behavior — should `continue` over holes with a bounded scan; (c) server.ex_dispatch_mask at 3191 is a self-described "legacy/unused" dead store — delete; (d) README.md:227 promises ex-queue-depth "pow2 ≤ 65536" but TOMO_EX_QUEUE_SIZE_MAX (server.h:1832) and the config upper bound are 2048 — fix the doc.
candidates.mechanism: Three independent sysfs parsers answering one machine-identity question is drift waiting to happen (they can already disagree: shared_cpu_list truncation at 63 chars vs level/id probing), and the two auto consumers (reply-bus count, pin policy) silently diverging by parser is exactly the 'invalid combo produced silently' class. The missing NOTICE means the single most topology-sensitive resolved value (num_cdb) is invisible in logs during sweeps — inconsistent with the knob doc's resolve-and-log pattern.
candidates.risk: Low. Pure boot-time refactor + logging; the hole-tolerant scan changes auto num_cdb only on boxes with offlined cores (arguably to the correct answer). Keep the g_multi_l3 read from the cached server field to avoid touching pin hot path (it's init-only anyway).

spsc_verify.reasoning: CONFIRMED. (1) flushExQueues (server.c:9753) has exactly two call sites: top of handleWorkerReplies (server.c:1953; reached only from beforeSleepIO server.c:2137 on IO threads iotid=1..io_threads-1, and beforeSleep server.c:2241 on main iotid=0) and tail of processInputBuffer (networking.c:4683; always on the thread owning the client, incl. the STALLED-resume at server.c:2126). No shutdown/cron/coordinator/worker caller exists; workers (exThreadMain server.c:10212) only pop and their iotid=TOMO_IO_THREADS_MAX+1+id would overflow queues[33] if they pushed — they never do. Flush indexes queues[iotid] via the thread-local, so it only ever touches the calling producer's own slot: a plain __thread bitmap word with zero atomics is sound. (2) The only writer of jobs[]/staged_tail is exQueuePush (9818/9824). Flush-dependent pushes are only the single-shard dispatches (server.c:5182, 5207). Every other flow — cross-shard subs (5770/5818), KEYS fan (5848), SETOP (5885), FLUSHALL sentinel (6034), migration fence sentinel (6219) — goes through csPushSpin (5717), which calls exQueuePush then IMMEDIATELY publishes tail=staged_tail (5722/5727), so those flows can only leave a benign stale-SET bit (staged==published, next flush no-ops), never a missed publish. freeback (9770) and the migration log (6085) are separate rings outside the bitmap's scope. (3) reshardCoordinator (6285) never calls flush and never reads staged_tail; its fence edges are the sentinel pop (immediate-publish csPushSpin, acked at 10344) and the 2ms idle heuristic reading published head/tail (6320-6328). It relies on publish TIMING, not on flush visiting all workers — the bitmap changes which queues get the release-store, never when a dirty queue gets it. (4) Same-thread sequencing makes the push-after-clear case safe: the re-set bit is consumed by the nested 4683 flush or the next pass's 1953 flush; even on the C_ERR early return (networking.c:4628-4630) that skips 4683, replyWorking (__thread, ae.c:34; incremented before every staged push, decrement requires publication) forces a 100µs poll (ae.c:482) so the next beforeSleepIO flush publishes within 100µs; on main, clients_pending_ex forces dont_sleep (2245). Supporting facts: tomokv-ex-threads/io-threads IMMUTABLE (config.c:3289-3290), num_workers set once (3301) and ≤64 (=TOMO_EX_THREADS_MAX, fits one word), queues inited once at startup (10642), no PARKED/spare balancer in this fork.
conditions: Set the bit on exQueuePush's SUCCESS path only (staged_tail advance at server.c:9824) or at all three caller sites (5182/5207/5720); the full/-1 return stages nothing. exQueuePush only receives exQueue* — the worker index must be derived (pointer arithmetic off server.exThreads) or passed in; a wrong queue->worker mapping is the one real way to lose a publish.

flushExQueues must clear a bit only at the visit that publishes that worker's queue, with no early exit between clear and the release-store (current loop body has none — keep it that way). Same-thread reentrancy is impossible today (flushExQueues calls nothing); do not add calls that can dispatch.

csPushSpin's direct tail publishes (server.c:5722/5727) leave stale-SET bits — must be tolerated as no-ops at the next flush visit (or optionally cleared there, which is also correct since staged==published on the same thread). They must never clear bits for other workers.

Bitmap must be per-producer-thread state (a __thread word, or a per-iotid slot touched only by its owner), >= num_workers bits; num_workers <= TOMO_EX_THREADS_MAX = 64 and is immutable, so one uint64_t suffices. Queues are initialized once at startup (server.c:10642) before serving, so no re-init/desync path exists.

Pre-existing, bitmap-NEUTRAL hazard to log (do not attribute to this change): the coordinator's 2ms idle heuristic (server.c:6320-6332) can ack a producer whose range write is staged-but-unpublished for >2ms (long inline/stateful call() at 5133/5215 executes before the networking.c:4683 flush), latching s_final early; the late-published write's log entry (seq>s_final) can be replayed by migDrainB (gate ph!=MIG_DONE, server.c:10272) over a fresher post-flip B write. Publish cadence is unchanged by the bitmap.

Pre-existing, bitmap-NEUTRAL: the C_ERR early return in processInputBuffer (networking.c:4628-4630) skips the eager 4683 flush; safety is the replyWorking>0 100us poll (ae.c:34, 482) plus the next pass's server.c:1953 flush — the bitmap preserves this exactly because the re-set bit survives until the next flush visit.
